title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1,000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2,000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, present the bootstrap CI as a preregistered descriptive summary, explicitly label a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations offers operational benefits but risks: sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can turn plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and empirical studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that degrade generated code and configurations [1],[2]. These failure modes motivate architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures (generate→validate→repair) to increase the likelihood of safe, deployable outputs.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our targeted research question is: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate), to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? By holding the initial generation constant, the estimand isolates the incremental effect of deterministic validation and at‑most‑one repair; it does not measure first‑pass prompt/decoding or sampling interventions.

Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1,000) with deterministic task selection from a synthetic stress corpus and archived validator traces; (2) full, artifact‑grounded confirmatory analysis of the preregistered primary estimand (exact two‑sided McNemar) and preregistered secondary descriptive summaries (paired bootstrap CI, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); and (3) an evidence‑based discussion of interpretation limits under shared_initial_candidate semantics and high baseline validity.
sections.related_work:
Empirical and survey literature shows LLMs produce factual and structural errors in code and structured outputs, with sensitivity to prompts and task framing [1],[2]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning have been shown to raise executable output rates in structured domains, though much evidence comes from non‑NetOps tasks and therefore depends on validator fidelity when transferred to networking [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system work argues for verifier‑assisted repair, digital‑twin validation, and protocol‑mediated governance to mitigate automation risks; these works present prototypes and benchmarked improvements in constrained settings but also emphasize that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and protocol enforcement rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Our study complements these prior works by strictly preregistering a paired estimand that attributes any paired outcome difference to downstream validation and the permitted repair call only (shared_initial_candidate). This design clarifies the separate contribution of a deterministic validator + bounded repair when initial-generation variance is removed.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The experiment preregistration (study id cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized and frozen prior to any hosted‑model invocation; the preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest is ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec. Key preregistered elements: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1,000 deterministic tasks sampled from challenging_workflow_stress_v1; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per pair deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as unsafe.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled initial candidate; the guarded pipeline may reject that candidate via deterministic validation and may invoke at most one permitted repair call. Therefore, paired outcome differences can arise only from deterministic validator decisions and permitted repair(s). This design does not measure effects that would have arisen from independent first‑pass generations, distinct prompts, or constrained decoding that were not executed under the frozen preregistration.

Model and runtime configuration. The declared provider/model in the archived configuration is gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset; we explicitly note that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The orchestration adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator version 5.0), a deterministic digital‑twin style emulator that enforces manifest constraints (required command presence and order, protected fields, group liveness constraints) and returns a binary safe‑deploy verdict.

Task corpus, selection, and scoring. Tasks include initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). The selection rule produced exactly 1,000 unique tasks deterministically. The validator applied the preregistered scoring_rule full_intent_constraint_validation to produce binary validity outcomes required for the paired analysis.

Execution accounting and missingness. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and prespecified missingness treatments. The adapter limited model calls per task to the preregistered bounds: exactly one shared initial generation per pair and at most one repair call for the guarded arm; missingness treatment for the primary analysis was complete_pair_primary as preregistered.

Analysis plan. The preregistered confirmatory procedure is an exact two‑sided McNemar test on the 2×2 paired contingency table. The paired bootstrap percentile interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was preregistered as a descriptive secondary summary. One‑sided tests were not prespecified; any one‑sided results are reported explicitly as exploratory/post‑hoc.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. The preregistered run completed as archived. Planned episodes = 2,000; completed = 2,000; complete_pairs = 1,000; failed episodes = 0. Total model calls used = 1,005 (shared_initial = 1,000; repair = 5); repair calls invoked = 5.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test. The 2×2 paired contingency counts are: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold, so the preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered secondary descriptive summaries and sensitivity. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01]. The bootstrap interval was preregistered as descriptive only; as discussed below, bootstrap percentile intervals can exclude zero under extremely sparse discordant counts even when an exact two‑sided McNemar is not significant. A one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) computed post‑hoc yields p = 0.03125; because a one‑sided McNemar was NOT prespecified in the frozen preregistration it is reported as exploratory/post‑hoc and does not alter the preregistered confirmatory conclusion.

Representative discordant pairs and repair modes. Five discordant pairs underlie the observed difference. The archived discordant pair identifiers and baseline failure codes are: pair‑000101, pair‑000253, pair‑000541, pair‑001117, pair‑001525. In each case the baseline episode failed validation (score_reason_code = VALIDATION_FAILED) on its single attempt and the guarded episode was accepted after the validator triggered the single allowed repair (guarded attempt_count = 2, score_reason_code = VALID_CONFIGURATION). These five pairs illustrate the guarded pipeline correcting ordering/sequence or protected‑field violations that the validator detected on the initial candidate; full per‑episode validator traces are archived with the run for forensic inspection. Only these five repair invocations produced paired differences.

Contamination and exclusions. The preregistered contamination and exclusion rules found no prompt‑leakage flags and no deterministic emulator errors; no post‑hoc exclusions were applied. All seeds and task_index selection rules were fixed pre‑execution per the preregistration.
sections.discussion:
Inferential hierarchy and bootstrap nuance. The preregistered confirmatory inference is the exact two‑sided McNemar test (p = 0.0625); because this test was preregistered and is the primary inferential gate, the formal confirmatory conclusion is that H1 is not supported at two‑sided α = 0.05. The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) is a preregistered descriptive summary and can exclude zero when discordant counts are extremely sparse: with n10 = 5 and n01 = 0, resampling of paired outcomes can produce nonzero percentile bounds despite the discrete exact McNemar p‑value crossing the prespecified α boundary. We report both results transparently and emphasize the preregistered McNemar as the confirmatory outcome; the bootstrap CI is informative about effect‑size sampling variability but does not override the preregistered two‑sided test.

Power assumptions and interpretation limits. The preregistered power plan assumed baseline ≈ 0.60 and targeted a 0.15 absolute increase. The observed baseline (0.995) is far higher than that assumption; this mismatch dramatically reduces the number of discordant pairs and therefore the sensitivity of the exact paired test to detect small absolute gains. Thus, failure to reach two‑sided significance should be interpreted in the context of near‑unity baseline validity and the paired design that isolates downstream effects only.

Mechanistic reading under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because the design reused the same initial candidate across conditions, paired gains can only come from deterministic validator decisions and the single allowed repair call. The five observed repairs show that a validator with suitable coverage can correct certain ordering/sequence violations; however, sparse repairs limit inference about repair efficacy across broader failure classes. Distinguishing whether the low repair count stems from high model correctness, corpus characteristics, or validator permissiveness requires follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, validator rule sets, repair budgets, and model families.

Threats to validity. Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary is determined by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate design isolates downstream effects but precludes measuring prompt/decoding interventions. External validity: the synthetic corpus and single declared model limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments. Conclusion validity: very few discordant pairs reduce test sensitivity in the observed regime.

Recommended preregistered follow‑ups (archive‑supported). To map practical utility, we recommend preregistered experiments that (a) remove shared_initial_candidate semantics to compare independent first‑pass generation arms (measure prompt/decoding effects), (b) sweep repair budgets (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns, (c) expand validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity, and (d) include multiple model families. Each follow‑up should align power calculations to plausible baseline failure prevalences.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1,000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1,005. The preregistered exact McNemar result is the formal confirmatory outcome; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified. Artifact‑grounded evidence indicates downstream verifier/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflows, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and repair budget. The archived preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts support reproducibility and preregistered follow‑ups to broaden model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

Preregistration: cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls; preregistration SHA‑256 recorded = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Full preregistration, execution manifests, raw model outputs, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
